        MOTION TO INTERVENE AND COMMENTS IN SUPPORT OF
                THE MISO TRANSMISSION OWNERS

       Pursuant to Rules 212 and 214 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s

(“Commission”) Rules of Practice and Procedure,1 the MISO Transmission Owners2

submit this motion to intervene and comments in support of the August 18, 2026 filing by

Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc. (“MISO”) in which MISO proposes

revisions to its Open Access Transmission, Energy and Operating Reserve Markets Tariff

 (“Tariff”) to create a Zero Injection Generator Interconnection Agreement (“ZGIA”),

related study process and operational requirements, and market and resource adequacy

rules to interconnect resources that intend to serve load, including large and co-located

loads, interconnected at the same substation and with the same voltage level as existing or

proposed load, i.e., Zero-Injection Generation (“ZG”) Resources.3 As explained in the

August 18 Filing and below, MISO’s proposal to create a new framework to accommodate

interconnection of ZG Resources will provide the region with another strategic and

operational tool to help meet the rapidly growing demand of large and co-located loads by

offering a streamlined interconnection pathway to resources that qualify, while also

formalizing an already existing practice, addressing aspects of the Commission’s directives

from its recent show cause order,4 and yielding independent benefits for the region’s

interconnection process. For these reasons, the Commission should accept the August 18

Filing’s proposed Tariff revisions, effective October 18, 2026.




3

       System Operator, Inc., Docket No. ER26-3552-000 (Aug. 18, 2026) (“August 18
       Filing”). All capitalized terms in this pleading that are not otherwise defined herein
       have the same meaning they are given in the current Tariff or the proposed Tariff
       revisions of the August 18 Filing.
4

 I.     COMMENTS IN SUPPORT

       A.      ZG Interconnection Service Will Provide the MISO Region With
               Another Efficient, Effective, and Tailored Tool to Address the Region’s
               Large Load Growth

       The MISO Transmission Owners support MISO’s proposed ZG Interconnection

Service construct as a just and reasonable framework that provides a limited, streamlined

interconnection path for a ZG Resource, i.e., a planned generator seeking to connect at the

same substation and with the same voltage level as existing or planned load, including large

loads and co-located loads.5     The proposed streamlined ZGIA framework, which is

specifically designed to complement MISO’s standard Interconnection Queue process, the

Definitive Planning Phase (“DPP”),6 establishes a targeted 90-day study process for

generation resources seeking a more limited interconnection service than Energy Resource

Interconnection Service (i.e., ERIS), which grants “as available” access to the full MISO

Transmission System.7 The ZGIA interconnection study process recognizes “the limited

distance over which energy would need to be—and is permitted to—flow,” allowing for a

more targeted and efficient study process.8       Load customers, including large load

customers, also will benefit from ZGIA interconnection studies that recognize on-site

generation, potentially reducing network upgrade requirements to interconnect. As MISO




5
       See August 18 Filing at 7.
6
       See id. at 14.
7
       See id. at 25; id., Tab C (Prepared Direct Testimony of Marc Keyser, Director,
       Central Region—External Affairs) at 7-8 (“Keyser Test.”).
8
       August 18 Filing at 25.

                                             3
 states, this framework “enables a pathway for certain large load configurations to achieve

speed to reliable power while maintaining system reliability.”9

       With its ZGIA proposal, MISO adds another tool to the region’s growing toolbox

for addressing the urgent and exponential load growth across the region. Specifically, the

ZGIA will complement MISO’s other recent strategic initiatives, including: the Expedited

Resource Addition Study, which provides a temporary accelerated interconnection process

tailored to generators needed within the region to serve important, near-term new load;

MISO’s improved Expedited Project Review (“EPR”) process, part of the MISO

Transmission Expansion Plan (“MTEP”), which expeditiously studies network upgrades

necessary for new large loads; and the MISO-Southwest Power Pool, Inc. (“SPP”) Joint

Targeted Interconnection Queue Study, which provides a pathway to build network

upgrades at the MISO-SPP seams.

       The crux of the proposed ZGIA framework is the new limited product, ZG

Interconnection Service,10 available for a Generating Facility that will only serve ZG

Associated Load,11 i.e., a designated load either at the same POI or has a POW12 on the

       load that has a Point of Withdrawal [(“POW”)] that is at the same substation as the
       Point of Interconnection [(“POI”)] to the Transmission System (i.e., same voltage

       Interconnection Service that will serve it”).
12
       POW is a new term proposed to be defined as “the point(s) where a non-
       transmission facility that is used to withdraw Energy from the Transmission System
       to serve Load connects to the Transmission System.” Id. at Attachment X. Put
       another way, POW is the “point that a Load interconnects to the Transmission
                                               4
 same voltage side of the same substation at the same voltage level, as identified in its

Interconnection Request.13 The ZG Interconnection study process, i.e., the ZG Impact

Assessment, will occur on an accelerated timeline, within ninety Calendar Days, at the end

of which MISO will issue a ZGIA to the parties. With an interconnection agreement, the

ZGIA Resource can then be modeled as an input to the subsequent MTEP (or MTEP EPR)

load study for its ZG Associated Load, potentially reducing the network upgrades needed

to integrate the new load.14

       MISO proposes requirements for eligibility of ZG Interconnection Service similar

to the requirements for standard Interconnection Service through its DPP process, but

includes additional requirements to allow MISO to study the generation in connection with

the ZG Associated Load and verify the ability of proposed configurations and control

equipment to limit injections, as required.15 Specifically, as MISO explains, the criteria

for a resource to qualify and proceed through the ZG Interconnection study process

deviates from MISO’s usual criteria for interconnection requests in five key ways:16

           (1) The Interconnection Customer must demonstrate a documented relationship
               with the planned or anticipated load to be connected at the same voltage
               side of the same substation, i.e., ZG Associated Load, and affirm the ZG


       System . . . the Load analog to the generation-specific term ‘Point of
       Interconnection’.” Keyser Test. at 23.

       ZGIA Interconnection Request process will use a serial “first-come, first-served”
       approach and will group ZGIA projects per cycle capping the number of requests
       per cycle to the first ten requests. Keyser Test. at 24. MISO proposes this deviation
       from the DPP process to prevent disruptions to the DPP process and ensure MISO
       maintains appropriate staffing levels. Id.

                                            5
                Associated Load’s intention to take service from the Interconnection
               Customer’s Generation Facility, i.e., the ZG Resource,17 using a ZGIA;

           (2) The Interconnection Customer requesting ZG Interconnection Service is not
               limited in the quantity of nameplate capacity of generation to be built, but
               is limited to receive only ZG Interconnection Service at a level that will not
               exceed peak demand of the ZG Associated Load, ensuring the maximum
               expected energy generated by the ZG Resource does not exceed maximum
               demand by the ZG Associated Load;18

           (3) When studying the Interconnection Request for ZG Interconnection
               Service, MISO will model the ZG Associated Load and confirm the
               proposed equipment sufficiently limits injections, which means MISO will
               study the load and generation together;19

           (4) The ZG Resource must interconnect at the same substation and voltage level
               as the POWs where the ZG Resource will serve the ZG Associated Load;20
               and

           (5) Study of the ZG Interconnection Service must find that the ZG Resource
               does not require Network Upgrades beyond the substation except for system
               protection facilities at adjacent substations.21

These enhanced requirements ensure that others on the Transmission System are not

negatively impacted by a ZG Resource.

       Moreover, a ZG Resource with an executed ZGIA will be subject to MISO’s

regional planning process and the specific local planning criteria of its appropriate

Transmission Owner.22 It also may participate in the replacement process for like resources

(i.e., replacing another Generating Facility that has ZG Interconnection Service in the same

 location), MISO’s resource adequacy construct, and the energy and operating reserve

       By proposing a new ZG Interconnection Service process that echoes MISO’s

standard interconnection process with slight variations, the ZG Interconnection Service

process adds consistency, transparency, and structure around these distinctive

interconnection requests to meet specific load needs.       Through its proposed ZGIA

framework, MISO will have a uniform process to account for actual impacts of these

resources with limited injections; ensure these Interconnection Customers pay for only the

necessary upgrades of their limited impacts; confirm the Interconnection Customer’s

proposed means for limiting injections; and memorialize and enforce the Interconnection

Customer’s commitments, including the control equipment and operational limitations, via

a binding ZGIA.24

       B.      ZG Interconnection Service Will Address the Show Cause Order’s
               Concern With Co-Located Load

       When discussing MISO’s lack of Tariff provisions regarding interconnection

service for generation serving co-located load, the Commission’s Show Cause Order

highlighted MISO’s development of a zero-injection generator interconnection process and

articulated a concern that such a process and its studies were not part of the Tariff.25

MISO’s proposal here, the culmination of that stakeholder-driven development, addresses

that concern. The proposed ZGIA framework is an adaptation of standard interconnection

service that aligns with directives of the Show Cause Order. Specifically, MISO’s proposal

 provides a solution to an aspect of the Commission’s concern about the lack of clarity and

consistency as to the rates, terms, and conditions of service that apply to interconnection

customers serving load that is geographically and electrically close, including co-located

load.26

          While MISO’s proposal slightly expands the definition of “co-location” envisioned

by the Show Cause Order,27 MISO reasonably determined, after extensive stakeholder

feedback,28 including from developers (such as developers of established or planned large

loads in the region),29 Transmission Owners, and other interested parties in the region, that

this broader scope, encompassing arrangements of load and generation not just at the same

POI, but generally located at the same substation with the same voltage level, better met

the region’s needs30 and struck an appropriate balance, offering a limited product with

limited impact on other projects and an accelerated study process.31 In addition to aligning

with stakeholder feedback, MISO found that defining a ZG Resource as serving load at the

same substation with the same voltage level would be “electrically indistinguishable”32

proximate,” or “co-located” behind the same POI, as described by the Show Cause Order.33

       Additionally, the Commission in the Show Cause Order highlighted the absence of

Tariff provisions that address the potential need for control equipment and protection

systems to ensure that an interconnection customer’s commitment to limit its generating

facility’s output to match the forecast of an electrically proximate large load or large co-

located load.34 MISO’s proposal includes strict limits on injections to the Transmission

System, which will limit the potential impacts to the Transmission System and need for

Network Upgrades,35 as well as requirements for control equipment and protection systems

as part of the proposed ZGIA.36

       MISO’s filing does not establish new rules regarding transmission service. As such

the ZG Associated Load must obtain transmission service to be served using the

Transmission System, which, for load served by a Load Serving Entity in MISO, is usually

Network Integration Transmission Service.37 Relatedly, MISO’s ZGIA filing does not

allow netting of load and generation for transmission service or market settlement

purposes.38 However, as described by MISO and highlighted in the request for abeyance

of the Show Cause Order’s deadlines by MISO and the MISO Transmission Owners,39 the

 proposed ZGIA framework is only one piece of MISO’s work plan for addressing all

aspects of the Show Cause Order and resolving the issues posed by the dramatic large load

growth in the region.40

       MISO’s proposed ZGIA framework would establish a uniform and tailored

interconnection service that will provide regional benefits to generation and load with

safeguards to avoid disruptions to the Transmission System and MISO’s current

interconnection process. It also addresses the Show Cause Order’s concerns regarding

generator interconnection service and the study of generation serving co-located load.

Accordingly, the Commission should accept MISO’s proposed ZGIA framework as just

and reasonable.

II.    MOTION TO INTERVENE

       This proceeding involves revisions to MISO’s Tariff to establish an entirely new

interconnection agreement, the ZGIA, the related processes and requirements for ZG

Resources, and provisions to integrate such resources as part of MISO’s market and

resource adequacy. As Transmission Owners within MISO that are subject to the Tariff,

each of the MISO Transmission Owners will be affected by whatever action the

Commission takes in this proceeding because the Tariff and its interconnection procedures

impact the MISO Transmission Owners’ transmission facilities. Additionally, the MISO

Transmission Owners have a vested interest in the MISO region’s ability to meet the need

for speed to power while maintaining resource adequacy and reliability as well as

 III.   CONCLUSION

       For these reasons, the MISO Transmission Owners request that the Commission

grant this motion to intervene and accept the August 18 Filing as just and reasonable,

effective October 18, 2026.
